title: 9x9 Opening & Joseki Explorer
description: Explore foundational 9x9 Fuseki (opening frameworks) and Joseki (settled corner exchanges) with standard Go terminology.

root.summary: On a compact 9x9 board, the center (Tengen) and the 3-3 / 3-4 / 4-4 points collide within 4–5 moves. Click any numbered marker to explore its branch.

children.summary: The strongest single-stone opening on 9x9. Radiates influence equally into all four corners and prevents the opponent from building a central wall.
White concedes central influence to Black's E5 stone in exchange for immediate, un-invadable corner territory in the bottom-left.
Black claims the opposite 3-3 corner while already holding E5—forcing White to split or approach immediately.
White takes the upper-left corner to build a left-side wall (C3–C7) facing Black's E5–G7 axis.
White takes the bottom-right corner, dividing the board diagonally (White: C3+G3, Black: E5+G7).
Aggressive contact play against White's 3-3 stone, using Black's E5 center stone as backup to start an immediate fight.
White stands up along the 3rd line to keep a base, inviting Black to press at D4.
White bends around the head of Black's D3 stone to contest the center—sharp tactical fighting!
Black approaches White's C3 corner from a distance while linking harmoniously with E5.
White plays on the 4th line to match Black's speed and influence rather than hunkering down on the 3-3 point.
Black mirrors on the upper-right 4-4 point, turning E5–F6 into a sweeping central diagonal.
Black dives straight into the 3-3 point underneath White's D4 stone—stealing the corner while White builds an outer wall.
Balances corner territory with directional facing toward the bottom side.
Secures the bottom-left corner in one move. Because two board edges act as free walls, White cannot easily live inside this corner.
White immediately claims the center of the board to stop Black from expanding out of C3.
Black claims the opposite corner, challenging White to prove that central thickness beats two secure corners.
Black extends along the bottom 3rd line to turn C3 into a broad side base.
White claims the diagonally opposite corner, leading to a balanced territorial race.
Black occupies the center point between both corners, controlling the flow of the midgame.
Black takes a third corner, daring White to invade the left side around C5.
One step off the 3-3 point—faces the bottom edge while leaving a 3-3 corner spot open for a follow-up enclosure.
White answers with speed and influence in the upper-right quadrant.
White takes the center to prevent Black from building a huge bottom-left moyo (framework).
White approaches Black's 3-4 stone immediately on the left side before Black can enclose the corner.
Prioritizes outward speed and center influence over immediate corner territory. Leaves the 3-3 point (C3) open.
Symmetric 4-4 battle—both players prioritize central thickness and fast development.
White dives directly into the 3-3 point beneath D4, trading outer thickness for solid corner cash.
